title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a genuine person is one who, even when not asked, speaks words not praising himself; what to say when asked! If asked and…
content: Furthermore, bhikkhus, a genuine person is one who, even when not asked, speaks words not praising himself; what to say when asked! If asked and required to answer, without hesitation or reluctance, he speaks words not praising himself fully and completely. This person, bhikkhus, should be understood as a genuine person. Furthermore, bhikkhus, a genuine person is one who, even when asked, does not speak words of praise for himself; what to say when not asked! If asked and required to answer, hesitantly and reluctantly, he speaks words of praise for himself, not fully, not completely. This person, bhikkhus, should be understood as a genuine person.

title: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as purified with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would…
content: Here, bhikkhus, knowing a person's mind as purified with my own mind, I understand: 'If this person were to die at this time, he would be reborn in heaven accordingly.' Why is that? Because his mind is purified. It is because of a purified mind, bhikkhus, that some beings here, after death, with the breakup of the body, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

title: Lohicca, if a person were to say: 'King Pasenadi of Kosala lives in Kasi-Kosala; let King Pasenadi of Kosala enjoy alone all the products of…
content: Lohicca, if a person were to say: 'King Pasenadi of Kosala lives in Kasi-Kosala; let King Pasenadi of Kosala enjoy alone all the products of Kasi-Kosala, no one else.' Would such a person be one who creates obstacles for those who depend on King Pasenadi of Kosala, or not? — Venerable Gotama, he would be one who creates obstacles. — Lohicca, being one who creates obstacles, does that person dwell with a mind of loving-kindness, wishing for the welfare of those others, or with a mind lacking loving-kindness? — Venerable Gotama, with a mind lacking loving-kindness. — Having a mind lacking loving-kindness, does that person dwell with a mind of loving-kindness or with a mind of harm? — Venerable Gotama, with a mind of harm! — Dwelling with a mind of harm, is that right view or wrong view? — Venerable Gotama, wrong view! — Lohicca, I say that a person with wrong view will be reborn in one of two lower realms: hell or the animal womb.

title: Elder Tissa: Abandoning a hundred bowls of gold and precious metal, I take an ordinary clay bowl. This is the second time I have been…
content:
Elder Tissa:

Abandoning a hundred bowls of gold and precious metal,
I take an ordinary clay bowl.
This is the second time I have been consecrated.

title: Bhikkhus, there are two kinds of teaching proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, one following the other. What two? 'See evil…
content:
Bhikkhus, there are two kinds of teaching proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, one following the other. What two? 'See evil as evil' — this is the first teaching. Having seen evil as evil, 'Be disenchanted, abandon it, be liberated from it' — this is the second teaching. Bhikkhus, these are the two kinds of teaching proclaimed by the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, one following the other.

By the Tathāgata, the Buddha,
Compassionate to all beings,
Two teachings are expounded
Step by step, Dhamma after Dhamma,
One following the other.

First, see evil as evil,
Then, being dispassionate toward it,
Abandon it completely.
From that, with mind dispassionate,
Make an end of suffering.

title: Kassapa, if a bhikkhu dwells cultivating a mind of compassion, without hatred, without malice, and with the destruction of the taints, he personally realizes and…
content: Kassapa, if a bhikkhu dwells cultivating a mind of compassion, without hatred, without malice, and with the destruction of the taints, he personally realizes and abides in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in this very life. That bhikkhu, Kassapa, is called a samaṇa, is called a brahmin.

title: Just as, bhikkhus, whatever streams flow into the great ocean and whatever rain falls from the sky, the great ocean does not thereby appear to…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, whatever streams flow into the great ocean and whatever rain falls from the sky, the great ocean does not thereby appear to decrease or increase. So too, bhikkhus, even if many bhikkhus attain final Nibbāna without remainder, Nibbāna does not thereby appear to decrease or increase. This, bhikkhus, is the fifth wonderful, marvelous quality in this Dhamma and Discipline. Seeing this, seeing this, bhikkhus delight in this Dhamma and Discipline.

title: Elder Sambhūta: One who, when he should go slowly, goes quickly, One who, when he should go quickly, goes slowly — That fool, lacking right…
content:
Elder Sambhūta:

One who, when he should go slowly, goes quickly,
One who, when he should go quickly, goes slowly —
That fool, lacking right method, goes to suffering.

His benefit diminishes like the moon in the dark fortnight.
He meets disgrace and opposes his friends.

One who, when he should go slowly, goes slowly,
One who, when he should go quickly, goes quickly —
That wise one, with right method, goes to happiness.

His benefit is fulfilled like the moon in the bright fortnight.
He gains fame and honor, not opposing his friends.

title: Here, bhikkhus, a person himself possesses faith and also encourages others to have faith; himself possesses moral shame and encourages others to have moral shame;…
content: Here, bhikkhus, a person himself possesses faith and also encourages others to have faith; himself possesses moral shame and encourages others to have moral shame; himself possesses moral dread and encourages others to have moral dread; himself is learned and encourages others to be learned; himself is energetic and encourages others to be energetic; himself is mindful and encourages others to be mindful; himself possesses wisdom and encourages others to possess wisdom. Such a person, bhikkhus, is called a genuine person even more than a genuine person.

title: Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor…
content: Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is no sloth and torpor in me.' And he understands how unarisen sloth and torpor arises; and he understands how arisen sloth and torpor is abandoned; and he understands how abandoned sloth and torpor will not arise in the future.
